purpose: Delete availability entries.
Mark a user unavailable for a period, so their tasks go to delegates.
notes: Needs a delegation first: without one 489 'User [<dn>] has no delegatee assignment configured for [cn=RequestDefs,…] provisioning request definitions.'. The real id (cn=<32 hex>,cn=DelegationDefs,…) is in POST /access/availability/list {dn}; dates come back rounded to seconds. Errors seen on the lab: for a user with no delegatee for the chosen requests → 489 'User [<DN>] has no delegatee assignment configured for [<request container>]…'.

purpose: Change an availability entry.
example: PUT …/access/availability {availabilityId, principalUser, effectiveDate, allRequests, hasExpiry, expiryDate}
notes: Same id; the list shows the new expiry.

purpose: List the availability entries of one user.

fields.name: dn
fields.values: DN of the user whose entries to list

answer: {availability:[{availabilityId, principalUser:{dn, name}, effectiveDate, expiryDate, hasExpiry, allRequests, enableAllRequests, availableRequestDefs:[{dn, name}], type:'DELEGATION_TYPE'}], totalAvailability, availabilityStatus, hasDelegatesAssigned, newable}
notes: With an availability entry for Alice: totalAvailability 1, availabilityStatus 1, hasDelegatesAssigned true; availableRequestDefs lists the PRDs her delegation covers (on the lab two: HelpDesk Ticket and Request Mobile Approval App). enableAllRequests was true right after the create and false a minute later. For Bob (the delegate, no entry of his own): totalAvailability 0, availabilityStatus 0, hasDelegatesAssigned false. Empty body or blank dn: 489 'Invalid input DN: null'. A DN that does not exist: 489 'User with dn [...] does not exist.'. Caller must be provisioning administrator or the user's team manager (AVAILABILITY). The dashboard's own list uses GET …/availability (no body) for the signed-in user. Errors seen on the lab: {} → 489 'Invalid input DN: null'; a DN that does not exist → 489 'User with dn [<DN>] does not exist.'.

purpose: List the PRDs a user may delegate when creating an availability.

params.name: userDn
params.values: user DN; omitted = signed-in user. Needs provisioning admin or team manager rights over that user

notes: Returns one template entry whose availabilityId is the placeholder 'apwaNewDetailId'; on the lab it carries no requestDefs (no delegable PRDs for uaadmin).

purpose: Set a user's overall availability status.

fields.name: status
fields.values: '0' (available) or '1' (unavailable) as seen in availability/list availabilityStatus; missing gives an HTML 500

answer: {status:'success'} on success; {} for a value it does not know; errors never change the HTTP 200
notes: SIDE EFFECT: it rewrites the user's availability entries. status '0' removed the existing dated entry; status '1' created a new open-ended all-requests entry (new id, hasExpiry false) that then had to be deleted. 'Available' answered {}; '2' answered success but availabilityStatus read 0. Missing status: HTML 500, rather than a validation message.

purpose: Page through the differences found by the last completed CPRS delta computation for a driver/entitlement.

params.name: source
params.values: filter by where the assignment was found (value passed to the stored delta search)

fields.name: driverDn
fields.values: DN of the driver whose entitlements are reconciled

fields.name: entitlementDn
fields.values: DN of one entitlement; omitted = all CPRS-mapped entitlements of the driver

fields.name: opType
fields.values: delta (compute differences), migrate (migrate assignments) or fetch

answer: {requestId, nextIndex, arraySize, deltaAssignmentsList:[{dn, firstName, lastName, entitlementDn, entitlementValue, logicalSystemId, source, instanceGuId, id}]}
notes: A read, but it only works after a reconcile with opType delta has completed for the same driver/entitlement/logical system; otherwise 489 'Delta computation might not have been perfomed…'. The lab has no CPRS-mapped resources (GET …/cprs/settings is empty) so no delta exists. If a request is still running and opType is fetch, the server refuses with 'request in progress'. CPRS must be enabled (GET …/administration/cprsConfig enableCprs) and the caller must be a Resources domain administrator. The dashboard also adds entitlementValues [{id}] to the body; the server's body type has no such field. 2026-10-31: while a delta run was still going the answer was 489 'Migration/delta computation in progress. Try again after some time'; the run never finished on the lab (see …/reconcile), so no delta was seen.

purpose: Turn selected delta rows into resource assignments (requests resources for each user).

fields.name: driverDn
fields.values: DN of the driver whose entitlements are reconciled

fields.name: entitlementDn
fields.values: DN of one entitlement; omitted = all CPRS-mapped entitlements of the driver

fields.name: opType
fields.values: delta (compute differences), migrate (migrate assignments) or fetch

notes: For each row the server finds the CPRS resources mapped to entitlementValue (or the dynamic-parameter resource) and requests them for the user; rows whose entitlement has no mapping are skipped. Published rows are removed from the stored delta (by id). The dashboard sends to …/reconcile instead when it is in migrate mode. CPRS must be enabled (GET …/administration/cprsConfig enableCprs) and the caller must be a Resources domain administrator.

purpose: Start a CPRS run (delta computation or migration) for a driver or one entitlement.

fields.name: driverDn
fields.values: DN of the driver whose entitlements are reconciled

fields.name: entitlementDn
fields.values: DN of one entitlement; omitted = all CPRS-mapped entitlements of the driver

fields.name: opType
fields.values: delta (compute differences), migrate (migrate assignments) or fetch

answer: {success:bool, succeeded:[{id: entitlement DN, requestId: DN under cn=CprsRequests}], failed:[{id, reason}]}
notes: Starts one CPRS request per mapped entitlement. Without a managedBy-1 resource for the entitlement: success false, 'Resource is not configured for permission reconciliation for entitlement …'. A second call while one runs: 'Delta Computation is already in progress for driver […]'. The run then waits for the driver to report the entitlement's current assignments; a driver without that support (a Loopback driver here) leaves it running (opStatus 1) and blocks further reconciles for that driver. CPRS must be enabled and the caller must be a Resources domain administrator.

purpose: Read the status of one CPRS request by its id.

fields.name: id
fields.values: CPRS request id returned by reconcile

answer: the request's status object {id, driverDn, entitlementDn, logicalSystem, opType, opStatus, statusMessage, counts, times}, or an empty 200 answer when the id is unknown
notes: With the id of a running request (from …/status/list) the server fails with 489 'Internal Error': it reads the completion time, which a running request does not have yet. An unknown or missing id answers 200 with no content. Only a finished request might work; none finished on the lab. Not used by the dashboard.

purpose: List past CPRS requests for a driver/entitlement, newest first.

params.name: sortBy
params.values: default requestCompletionTime; a CPRS request column name

answer: {cprsRequestStatus:[{id, driverDn, entitlementDn, opType, opStatus, totalAssignments, failedAssignments, requestStartTime, requestCompletionTime}], nextIndex, arraySize, total}
notes: An empty body {} → 489 'Internal Error'; give driverDn (entitlementDn alone answered nothing). opStatus 1 = running (requestCompletionTime empty). Unlike the other CPRS calls this one does not require CPRS to be enabled, only Resources domain administrator. Errors seen on the lab: {} with sortBy empty → 489 'Internal Error. Please contact Administrator.'.

purpose: List the entitlement-value to resource mappings used by CPRS.

params.name: column
params.values: columns to include: drivername, logicalsystem, entitlement, entitlementvalue, resource (dashboard column keys)

answer: {cprsSettingList:[{drivername, logicalsystem, entitlement, entitlementvalue, resource, id}], nextIndex, arraySize, total}
notes: Resources domain administrator only. Lists resources with managedBy 1 (set with PUT …/catalog/resources/resource) that are bound to a cprs-supported entitlement; a resource bound to such an entitlement but with managedBy 0 is not listed. entitlementvalue is the stored value (compact JSON for a query entitlement).

purpose: Delete delegations.
Delegate one user's tasks to another.

fields.name: createAvailability
fields.values: bool; read without a null check

answer: the request echoed with assignmentId 'apwaNewDetailId' (a placeholder, not the new id)
notes: The answer does not give the real id; read it from POST /access/delegation/list {dn:<from user>} (cn=<32 hex>,cn=DelegateeDefs,…). No expiry is stored as 4102444799000. The delegation shows under both users.

purpose: Change a delegation.
notes: The id stays the same; the list shows the new expiry.

purpose: List the request categories offered when choosing which requests to delegate.
notes: Lab categories: entitlements, nrf (Roles), attestation, groups, accounts. Category ids are per installation (PRD categories). Caller must be the provisioning administrator, a team manager with delegation rights, or a PRD domain delegated administrator.

purpose: List the delegation assignments of one user.
answer: {delegations:[{assignmentId, isExpires, allRequests, assignFromUsers:[{dn, name}], assignToUsers:[{dn, name}], expiryDate, type:'DELEGATEE_TYPE'}], totalDelegations}
notes: With a delegation from Alice to Bob, the same entry shows for both dn=Alice and dn=Bob (the list covers delegations from and to the user). No expiry is stored as 4102444799000. Empty body: 489 'Invalid input DN: null'. Query parameters are not read (the dashboard only adds size). The signed-in user's own list is GET …/delegation (q, nextIndex, size, sortBy, sortOrder). Errors seen on the lab: {} → 489 'Invalid input DN: null'; a user that was deleted → 489 'User with dn [<DN>] does not exist.'.

purpose: List the relationships a delegation can target instead of named users.
notes: Lab: one relationship, key manager. Keys are per installation.

purpose: List PRDs, optionally limited to one request category, for choosing delegated requests.

params.name: category
params.values: categoryId from GET …/delegation/category; empty = all PRDs

notes: Lab: no category → 8 PRDs; nrf → 4; accounts → 2; an unknown category → {arraySize:0}, no error. Caller must be the provisioning administrator, a team manager with delegation rights, or a PRD domain delegated administrator.

purpose: Render a request, approval or workflow-template form as form.io JSON.

params.name: formContainer
params.values: RequestForms, ApprovalForms or TemplateForms (compared case-insensitively); required

params.name: pid
params.values: PRD DN: required for RequestForms; for TemplateForms the template PRD DN (alternative to id)

params.name: id
params.values: for ApprovalForms the task id (required); for TemplateForms the form DN (alternative to pid)

params.name: proxyFor
params.values: ApprovalForms: user DN to act for

answer: {formJSON: string (a form.io definition, serialized JSON; ~205 KB for the template form, ~22 KB for the help-desk request form)}
notes: Errors: no formContainer → 489 'Form Container is Empty.'; TemplateForms with neither id nor pid → 489 'Invalid Input for Template forms…'; RequestForms without pid → 489 'Invalid input DN: '; id given as a bare name → 489 'Failed to generate form'. An unknown container → 204 with no body. RequestForms also checks that the caller may request that PRD. Verified on the lab: TemplateForms by id and by pid (cn=NoApproval template), RequestForms with pid=HelpdeskTicket PRD. ApprovalForms was not tried (no open task on the lab). The dashboard opens the form renderer with these parameters rather than calling it directly.

purpose: List the data-item fields a stored form exposes.

params.name: formId
params.values: full form DN (not the bare name); required

notes: No formId → 489 'Form ID is empty.'; a bare form name → 489 'Internal Error'. Provisioning domain administrator only. Comment fields are left out. Errors seen on the lab: formId=Create Workflow Form (a template form) → 489 'Internal Error. Please contact Administrator.'.

purpose: List the PRD templates used to create new workflows.

params.name: isCustom
params.values: false (default) = built-in approval templates; true = custom templates

notes: Lab: 9 built-in templates (No Approval, Single Step, Two/Three/Four Step Serial and Parallel, …); isCustom=true → {size:0}. Provisioning domain administrator only.

purpose: List the stored workflow forms of one container.

params.name: formContainer
params.values: container name, required: TemplateForms, RequestForms, ApprovalForms seen; the value picks the form container

notes: No formContainer → 489 'Form Container is Empty.'. Lab: TemplateForms → 1 form (Create Workflow Form); RequestForms → request forms; ApprovalForms → approval forms. An unrecognised value (e.g. bogus) returned the approval forms rather than an error. Provisioning domain administrator only.

purpose: Read the comments of one workflow request.

params.name: sortOrder
params.values: asc or desc (default desc); anything else → 489 'Invalid sort order'

answer: {listCommentNode:[{commentId, requestId, activityId, activityName, author, authorType, messageId, commentText, createTime, sequenceNumber, isSystemComment, activityType}]}
notes: No requestId → 489 'Invalid requestId'. Ids from historylist and from process/list both work. An id that is not a workflow request id (e.g. a role request's correlation id) gives 489 'Error retrieving comment details.' rather than an empty list. A terminated process lists the terminate comment first. Errors seen on the lab: sortOrder=bogus → 489 'Invalid sort order: bogus'.

purpose: List workflow processes (requests) for monitoring, with filters.

params.name: q
params.values: search text; '*' or omitted = all; matched on a field other than the process name (q=Role, q='Add Role' gave 0)

params.name: operator
params.values: comparison for creationTime: GT worked; '>' was ignored

params.name: processStatus
params.values: status display name, e.g. Completed (numeric codes are ignored)

params.name: approvalStatus
params.values: approval display name, e.g. Approved (numeric codes are ignored)

params.name: sortField
params.values: database column name in capitals, e.g. CREATION_TIME; other names (creationTime, name) → 489 database error

answer: {processInfoNodeList:[{requestId, processId, version, name, creationTime, completionTime, recipient, recipientName, initiator, initiatorName, processStatus, processStatusDisplayName, approvalStatus, approvalStatusDisplayName, correlationId, engineId, …}], totalSize:int}
notes: No parameter is required. totalSize was 20 for the unfiltered list and 17 with processStatus=Completed; creationTime=…&operator=GT narrowed it to 2. A wrong sortField gives 489 'An error occurred while obtaining the process or comment details from the database'. 2026-10-31: the list returned one row fewer than totalSize (21 of 22; running: 1 of 2), and the missing one was a just-created process, so a new process may not be listed. A recipient filter (recipient=<user DN>) answered 489, alone or with processStatus; sortField=creationTime with sortOrder=desc also answered 489.

purpose: Terminate running workflow processes.

fields.name: processes
fields.values: list of request ids to stop

fields.name: primaryPrincipal
fields.values: ignored; the server sets the caller

notes: Terminated a role approval process (requestId from GET …/monitoring/process/list): its processStatus became 2 and the comment was recorded, but its approval task stayed in GET /access/tasks/list and the role request stayed 'Approval Pending' (as after a retraction). Only processes is checked (missing → 489 'Invalid request'). Not used by the dashboard.

purpose: Reassign workflow tasks to another user.
example: POST …/monitoring/reassign {afTaskNode:{tasks:[{taskId:"<task id>", addressee:"<new addressee DN>"}], comment:"<text>"}}
notes: The new addressee goes in afTaskNode.tasks[].addressee: {afTaskNode:{tasks:[{taskId, addressee: new addressee DN}], comment}}. That moved the task (assignStatus REASSIGNED, comment 'User task reassigned to reviewer …'). Careful: other shapes also answer {success:true} and do nothing (afTaskNode as a single task, a primaryPrincipal, an approver field), one of them claimed the task for the caller, and afTaskNode.tasks with an approver field and no addressee failed with an HTML 500. Not used by the dashboard.

purpose: List the work entries (tasks/activities) of one request.
answer: {workentries:[{activityId, activityName, addressee, assignmentType, availableActions:[…], creationTime, id: task id, owner, priority, processId, …}], totalSize}
notes: requestId is the workflow request id (requestId from GET …/monitoring/process/list), not the role request's DN or a task id (those answered {totalSize:0}). For an open approval: the task with addressee, owner (Unclaimed), availableActions and priority.

purpose: Read the proxy settings: notification template and retention time.
notes: The global proxy setting (notification template, retention), not the list of proxies (those read from GET /access/proxy/all). {} until one is set; after POST {proxyRetentionTime:60} it read {proxyRetentionTime:60}. Allowed for a team manager or anyone with the delegation/proxy configuration right. Retention is stored in ms and returned in minutes.

purpose: Save the proxy notification template and retention time.

fields.name: proxyRetentionTime
fields.values: minutes; negative → error 'negative values not allowed'

notes: Both fields optional; only those present are saved (proxyRetentionTime alone worked). Empty body → error. Needs the delegation/proxy configuration right.

purpose: Make a user a proxy for other users.

fields.name: assignedUserDN
fields.values: the user who becomes the proxy

fields.name: proxyForUsers / proxyForGroups / proxyForContainers
fields.values: at least one non-empty list of {dn}

fields.name: expirytime
fields.values: epoch ms as string; leave it out (or empty) for no expiry. '-1' is taken as a date in 1969 and refused

fields.name: notificationAddresseeType
fields.values: with notification: ALL, ASSIGN_FROM, ASSIGN_TO, SELECTIVE

answer: {proxyDefinitions:[{dn, proxyForUsers:[{dn, username}], assignedUserDN, assignedUserName, editable, expirytime}], configureProxy}
notes: No expiry is stored as 4102444799000 (end of 2099). expirytime '-1': 489 SecurityException 'Invalid proxy definition … Expiration time is prior to current time.'. The id is cn=<32 hex>,cn=ProxyDefs,cn=AppConfig,…. Errors seen on the lab: with expirytime '-1' → 489 'Invalid proxy definition. Definition: …'.

purpose: Delete proxy definitions.
notes: A POST that deletes. GET /access/proxy/all empty afterwards.

purpose: Change a proxy definition.

fields.name: dn
fields.values: definition id from proxy/create or GET /access/proxy/all

notes: GET /access/proxy/all showed the new expiry.

purpose: Read the proxy/delegation background service schedule.
answer: {cleanUpSeviceActivationInteval:int, syncServiceActivationInterval:int, lastCleanUpDate?:epoch ms, scheduledCleanUpDate?:epoch ms, cleanupChoice:'useInterval'|'useDate'}
notes: Field names keep the vendor misspelling (cleanUpSeviceActivationInteval). Lab: both intervals 0, cleanupChoice useInterval. cleanupChoice is useDate when a cleanup date is scheduled. Needs the delegation/proxy configuration right.

purpose: Save the proxy/delegation service schedule.

fields.name: cleanupChoice
fields.values: useInterval or useDate; must be present (read without a null check)

fields.name: cleanUpSeviceActivationInteval
fields.values: minutes; used when cleanupChoice is useInterval

fields.name: scheduledCleanUpDate
fields.values: epoch ms in the future; used otherwise (a past date → 'invalid cleanup date')

notes: cleanupChoice is required (read without a null check). Posting the GET answer back (all zeros on the lab) left it identical. The server multiplies the minute values by 60000 when saving and the GET does not convert back, so with non-zero values a save of the GET answer would multiply them; convert first (not checked with non-zero values).

purpose: Remove a whole cart.

fields.name: cartOwner
fields.values: the caller's DN or omitted (any other DN is refused)

notes: Deletes the caller's whole cart for that cartAction; GET afterwards: totalCount 0. Worked at once (0.1 s) after the applications were restarted. Before, every call hung until the client gave up (120 s, then an nginx 504): an earlier item delete had left an uncommitted database transaction in one server worker, whose lock the cart delete waited on. If this call hangs, look for such a transaction (or restart).

purpose: Read the signed-in user's cart for one cart action, with its items.

params.name: cartAction
params.values: required, free text; the cart's action name (e.g. revoke)

params.name: cartOwner
params.values: optional; only the caller's own DN is accepted

answer: {cartOwner, cartAction, totalCount:int, cartItems?:[{itemDn, itemType, itemAssignees:[{instanceId, subtype, assignedToDn}]}]}
notes: Missing cartAction → 489 'Value for cartAction is missing in payload…'. Another user's cartOwner → 489 'You are unauthorized for this operation.'. After a restart of the applications, 20 reads in a row all answered 200 (the earlier 1-in-20 489 was the hung transaction, see DELETE). Errors seen on the lab: while the cart transaction hung, about 1 call in 20 → 489 'Internal Error. Please contact Administrator.' (gone after a restart).

purpose: Remove assignees from cart items.
notes: The item stays in the cart without assignees.

purpose: Remove items from a cart.
answer: {success, succeeded:[{id}]} or success false 'Error in deleting queue item <dn>'
notes: UNRELIABLE on the lab: for the 1st item it answered success but other workers kept showing the item (the delete was left uncommitted, see DELETE /access/queue/entry); a repeat answered success false 'Error in deleting queue item'. For the 2nd item it worked at once. Cart writes also need the item DN to be an existing permission ('Permission with id […] does not exist.').

purpose: Add items (permission + assignees) to the caller's cart.

fields.name: cartAction
fields.values: the cart's name, free text chosen by the client

notes: A cart is per (owner, cartAction); a scratch cartAction name kept the real carts (revoke, request) untouched. GET /access/queue/entry?cartAction=<name> reads it; totalCount counts assignees, not items. Errors seen on the lab: a role that was deleted → 489 'Permission with id [<DN>] does not exist.'; while the cart transaction hung, a call timed out with no answer.

purpose: The signed-in user's request history (PRD, role and resource requests), newest first.
notes: Lab: always 489 'Failed to get process request history', with or without parameters. The server merges PRD history with role/resource history and fails as a whole if either part fails. Use GET or POST …/requests/historylist instead. The dashboard uses this path only with DELETE, to retract requests. 2026-10-31, after a restart: still 489. The workflow engine fails while writing the PRD-history part of the answer and closes the connection mid-answer, so the call fails as a whole: a server fault, not an input problem. A server bug, not an input problem.

purpose: Request history of another user, for administrators and authorised help-desk users.

params.name: sortBy
params.values: default requestDate; requestState sorts by status

params.name: type
params.values: prd, role or resource; anything else (default *) = all three

params.name: action
params.values: request action filter; default *. PRD history is included only when action is *

fields.name: dn
fields.values: DN of the user whose history to read

answer: {totalSize:int, total:int, nextIndex:int, requests:[{id, name, entityType, requestState, processState, status, requester, requesterName, requesterType, recipient, recipientName, recipientType, requestDate, confirmationNumber, retractable}]}
notes: No dn → 489 'User DN is required in the payload'. Allowed for a domain administrator, or a help-desk user whose client list includes the user's client. Lab: 20 requests for uaadmin. After POST …/administrator/assignments/create made a user a delegated role administrator, the user's role history showed a 'Role Manager' request (Completed): the admin assignment is itself a role assignment.

purpose: PRD request history of the signed-in user, or of the user they act as proxy for.

params.name: sortBy
params.values: default requestDate; requestState sorts by status

fields.name: dn
fields.values: user DN the caller acts for (proxy); the caller's own DN gives their own history

answer: {totalSize:int, total:int, nextIndex:int, requests:[{id, name, entityType, requestState, processState, status, requester, requesterName, requesterType, recipient, recipientName, recipientType, requestDate, confirmationNumber, retractable}]}
notes: Despite the body being named 'proxy user', a body is needed: {} → 489 'Cannot validate user authentication info'; no body → HTTP 400 (HTML page). Only PRD (workflow) requests are listed. GET …/requests/historylist (same query parameters, no body) returns the caller's own list and is what gave the request ids used here.

purpose: Submit requests for roles, resources or PRDs, for oneself or for recipients.

fields.name: reqPermissions
fields.values: non-empty list of {id, entityType, proxyFor}; entityType role, resource or prd

fields.name: recipients
fields.values: list of {dn, type (user/group/…), isGroupAssignment, targetSetList}; omitted = request for the caller

fields.name: process
fields.values: workflow callback data (used when called from a workflow)

answer: {success, OperationNodes:[{success, succeeded:[{id, instanceId: request DN}], userDn}]}
example: POST …/requests/permissions {reason, reqPermissions:[{id:"<role DN>", entityType:"role"}], recipients:[{dn:"<user DN>", type:"user"}]}
notes: Requested a role with an approval for another user: success, and the approver got a task. Group recipients are expanded; groups are kept as group assignments only for Roles or Security domain administrators.

purpose: List resource categories for the request catalog.

params.name: sortBy
params.values: name only (default); anything else → invalid sort column

params.name: token
params.values: cache token from a previous answer; reuses the cached list

params.name: noCache
params.values: default false; true skips the cache

params.name: forceRefresh
params.values: default false; with a token, true drops that cached list first

notes: Lab: default, helpdesk, system. Category ids are per installation. forceRefresh only clears a cached copy for that token; it was not used.

purpose: List role categories for the request catalog.

params.name: sortOrder
params.values: desc sorts descending; anything else ascending (not validated)

notes: Lab: default, system. Unlike resourceCategories, an invalid sortOrder is accepted silently.

purpose: Request history of a team member, for team managers.

params.name: sortBy
params.values: default requestDate; requestState sorts by status

params.name: type
params.values: prd, role or resource; anything else (default *) = all three

params.name: action
params.values: request action filter; default *. PRD history is included only when action is *

answer: {totalSize:int, total:int, nextIndex:int, requests:[{id, name, entityType, requestState, processState, status, requester, requesterName, requesterType, recipient, recipientName, recipientType, requestDate, confirmationNumber, retractable}]}
notes: No dn → 'User DN is required'. Allowed for a team manager or domain administrator; each type (prd/role/resource) is included only if the caller manages or administers that domain. As domain administrator uaadmin the answer matched historyForUser.

purpose: List the workflow tasks of one member of a team the caller manages.

params.name: sortOrder
params.values: asc or desc; otherwise 489 'Invalid sort order'

params.name: status
params.values: only Claimed is accepted; any other value → 489 'Invalid task status'

notes: The team needs the task permission on the PRD the task belongs to: PUT /access/teams/permissions with {dn: PRD DN, objClass: srvprvRequest, permission: nrfAccessMgrTaskAddressee} ('Manage Addressee Task'). Without it the call answers 200 with total 0 even though the member has tasks; with it, the member's role approval task was listed. The caller must be a team manager and the member must belong to one of the caller's teams, else 489 'You are unauthorized for this operation.'. Missing memberDn or teamDN: 489 'Team member input is empty…'. Errors seen on the lab: teamId instead of teamDN, or no memberDn → 489 'Team member input is empty, please input team member detail'; a team that does not exist → 489 'You are unauthorized for this operation.'; status=bogus → 489 'Invalid task status'.

purpose: Delete teams.
notes: Afterwards GET /access/teams/list?forceRefresh=true is empty and POST /access/teams/team {dn} answers 489 'Internal Error' (not a not-found message).

purpose: Create a team (managers, members, domains).

fields.name: recipients
fields.values: members [{dn, type}]; type user, group, container or relationship; required unless allUsers

answer: the team: {name, dn, description, recipients, requestors, allUsers, includeManager, localizedNames, localizedDescriptions, readOnly, domainTypes}
notes: The DN is generated: cn=<name without dashes><32 hex>,cn=TeamDefs,cn=AppConfig,…. Without domainTypes all three domains are set.

purpose: Change a team.

fields.name: recipients / allUsers
fields.values: not both: allUsers true with recipients gives 489 'All Users are already selected for the team recipients.'

example: PUT …/access/teams {dn, name, description, requestors, recipients, allUsers:false}
notes: POST /access/teams/team {dn} showed the new description.

purpose: List resources under one resource container (for picking team permissions).

fields.name: dn
fields.values: container DN to search under; empty = the default root

notes: A read despite POST. The search filter is applied in memory on name and description.

purpose: List roles under one role container (for picking team permissions).

fields.name: dn
fields.values: container DN to search under; empty = the default root

notes: {"dn":""} gave the same first page as the level-20 container. The dashboard calls it with {dn: role sub-container} when the widget is limited to one.

purpose: List the teams the caller manages, optionally only those with one permission.

params.name: type
params.values: team type; empty (default) or A = all; the dashboard sends A. ALL, PROVISIONING and other values gave 489 'Internal Error'

params.name: pType
params.values: permission the caller must hold on the team, e.g. AVAILABILITY (a permission-type name)

params.name: sortOrder / forceRefresh
params.values: sent by the dashboard in some modes; not read by the server

answer: {teams:[{name, dn, allUsers, includeManager, readOnly}], arraySize, totalCount, nextIndex}
notes: Lists the teams the caller manages (uaadmin is a team manager of the test team). type=A, type=R and no type all gave the same one team; totalCount came back 0 even with one team (only arraySize is reliable). When the caller manages no team the answer is 489 'No Teams found with Manage Addressee Permission' (the generic empty-list message). Errors seen on the lab: no team with that permission → 489 'No Teams found with Manage Addressee Permission'; type=ALL → 489 'Internal Error. Please contact Administrator.'.

purpose: List the members of the teams that contain a given member and that the caller manages.
notes: Returns the members of every team the CALLER manages; memberDn must be present but its value is not used (Alice's DN and uaadmin's DN gave the same list). Alice and Bob came back. A caller who manages no team: 403 'Team manger does not belong to any Team'. Without memberDn: 489 'Internal Error' (the server tests the value before checking it is present). Errors seen on the lab: no memberDn → 489 'Internal Error. Please contact Administrator.'; memberDn of a manager without teams → 403 'Team manger does not belong to any Team' (sic).

purpose: Remove team permissions.
notes: Same shape as the grant; team/permissions read empty afterwards.

purpose: List the permissions the caller may request for others through their teams.

fields.name: useExcludePermList
fields.values: bool; true also applies the teams' exclusion lists

notes: Still {nextIndex:0, arraySize:0} although the team holds Assign/Revoke Role on a role (shown by /teams/team/permissions and /admin/permission/assignment), with q * or the role's name and with useExcludePermList true or false. The server builds this list from a vault search plus the permission index, filtered by the request operation 'grantToUser'; why the role grant did not appear was not found. PRD grants (nrfAccessMgrInitiatePRD) were not tried, because granting on a PRD writes to a PRD object the test did not create. A read despite POST (the dashboard's request-on-behalf permission list). {} and an empty targetSetDnList answer {nextIndex:0, arraySize:0}. Re-tried 2026-10-31 after a restart (the permission index is rebuilt then) and with the team also holding Initiate PRD and Manage Addressee Task on a PRD: still empty.

purpose: Grant a team permissions on roles, resources or PRDs.

fields.name: permissions[].dn
fields.values: the role, resource or PRD (or container) DN

fields.name: permissions[].permission
fields.values: an access key from GET /admin/permission?domain=ROLES|RESOURCES|PROVISIONING, e.g. nrfAccessMgrAssignRole, nrfAccessMgrRevokeRole

notes: The permission key is NOT checked: 'AssignRole' (the dashboard's checkbox id) also answered success but was invisible in POST /access/teams/team/permissions; it was removed with the matching DELETE. With nrfAccessMgrAssignRole the grant appears there (permissionDisplay 'Assign Role To User'). PRD grants work too: {dn: PRD DN, objClass: srvprvRequest, permission: nrfAccessMgrTaskAddressee or nrfAccessMgrInitiatePRD} (they write to the PRD object); the matching DELETE removed them.

No teamDn: 489 'Team DN input is empty…'; a DN that is not a team: 489 'Internal Error'. Errors seen on the lab: no teamDn → 489 'Team DN input is empty, please input team dn detail'; a team DN that does not exist → 489 'Internal Error. Please contact Administrator.'.

purpose: Create a PRD (workflow) from a built-in approval template for a role or resource.

fields.name: template
fields.values: template PRD DN from GET …/forms/listTemplates; must exist

fields.name: cn
fields.values: new PRD cn; must be valid for a DN

fields.name: prdName
fields.values: localized names [{key: locale, value}]; must be valid

fields.name: processType
fields.values: Normal, or Role Approval (for Role) / Resource Approval (for Resource)

fields.name: permissionDN
fields.values: role/resource DN; required when processType is Normal

notes: approveInfo (a list of approval steps {approvalFormDN, approvalOrder, approvers:[DN], approversType}) is needed even for the No Approval template: without it the workflow engine fails ('approvalNodeList' is null). With it, the engine builds the PRD and then calls back into the applications to store it; on the lab that call never reached the applications (not in the access log) and the answer was 489 'Failed to create the PRD.'. That matches the lab's known problem with the workflow engine's own sign-in to the applications, so this is likely a lab configuration issue. Provisioning administrator only; an existing PRD with the same cn → error. Use POST …/access/workflow/prd to store a PRD from its XML.

purpose: Create a PRD from raw process-flow and request XML.

fields.name: prdName
fields.values: localized names [{key, value}]; iterated without a null check

fields.name: prdDescription
fields.values: localized descriptions [{key, value}]; iterated without a null check

example: POST …/workflow/prd {prdCN, prdName:[{key:"en", value}], prdDescription:[{key:"en", value}], prdCategory:"<category>", prdStatus:"Active", xmlData:"<prov-req-defn …>", requestXML:"<provision-request …>"}
notes: Stores a PRD from its XML: xmlData = the PRD definition (<prov-req-defn …>, as in a Designer or vault PRD) and requestXML = its request form XML. Tested with a copy of a template's definition (new prov-id, status Active, category accounts): GET …/catalog/prds listed the new PRD at once. Only an empty body is rejected explicitly; prdName and prdDescription are iterated without a null check, so send both.

purpose: For administrators: every request made for one role, resource or PRD.
notes: The permission goes in the item query parameter. With id or permissionId (query or body) it answers 489 'Permission id (id:) is required', which misled earlier attempts.
